tasks.short: Maintain complete and accurate pupil records

steps.what: Gather and check actual student observations and required source information
Enter required student record fields and source references
Write the factual student record narrative from checked observations

loop.purpose: Draft factual wording for the existing record
loop.input: Teacher's checked observations and source references
loop.output: Draft narrative with an observation source for each statement
loop.check: Teacher checks meaning, chronology, attribution and uncertainty; remove inferred diagnoses or unsupported judgements
loop.stop: Missing evidence or changed meaning requires manual writing; one redraft maximum
loop.why_not_simpler: Irregular factual observations need prose rather than only fixed fields

steps.what: Check the student record for completeness and factual accuracy
Save the student record in its existing record screen

tasks.design: Configure required fields and source links in the existing pupil record tool {OTHER} before adding a bounded factual narrative draft. The teacher captures the actual evidence, checks all meaning and completeness, and saves the ordinary internal record without a new approval stage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stable pupil and source references are repeated and factual notes are rewritten into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms handle stable fields; a small source-bound drafting step can handle irregular prose.
tasks.still_hard: A complete-looking record may contain an inaccurate or unsupported statement.
tasks.human_edge: Know the child and distinguish actual observations from assumptions.

ambition.what: The teacher retains responsibility for the record's accuracy.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: required-field forms and source-bound narrative drafting can reduce repeated record entry while factual checks remain necessary.

assumptions: Boundary is actual routine pupil record maintenance, used by the teacher and authorized school staff. Formal grade release, educational placement decisions and external reports are distinct actions, not ordinary saves automated here.

The teacher produces observations and checks existing pupil evidence in s1; school administration supplies pupil id and the record owner supplies required field definitions. Missing source references are entered manually within retained work; extra extraction and repair are funded below.

s2 removes nine units of repeated identifiers, stable fields and source-reference navigation, retaining twenty-one for actual facts, corrections and checks. s3 retains17.5 of25 for reviewing and correcting prose plus the full nineteen-unit final accuracy check.

Native forms and existing note templates are tested first. Existing system runtime earns no benefit. Same-system save is tiny, fully retained and ungated; s4 is factual checking, not self-approval to save. Shares are illustrative.
unknowns: Which record fields are actually repeated today
Whether narrative drafting saves time after full semantic review
research_questions: Does every draft sentence trace to the teacher's actual evidence?

already_counted.description: Gather actual evidence, enter facts, check narrative meaning and completeness and save

incremental.description: Maintain required fields and source mappings and repair difficult drafts

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R83.5 gross16.5 less upkeep3 gives13.5. With changed record requirements and largely bespoke observations, field entry retains28 of30 and narrative23 of25; source25, final check19 and save1 stay. R96 gross4 less upkeep3 gives1.

tasks.short: Enforce school rules in daily interactions

steps.what: Read the relevant administration policy or student rule when clarification is needed
Enforce administration policies and rules through direct student interaction

tasks.design: Link the current student rules in {DOCS} for occasional clarification. The teacher observes the situation and applies the rule in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: A policy clarification can require searching among older documents.
tasks.enabler_now: A native current-version link can remove that small navigation cost.
tasks.still_hard: Consistent and proportionate enforcement depends on the situation and the student.
tasks.human_edge: De-escalate, explain boundaries and exercise sound judgement.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: current-version policy links can reduce occasional lookup time; live classroom rule enforcement remains human.

assumptions: Representative episode is a routine classroom rule reminder, not a formal disciplinary case. No log is invented for every reminder. A real recorded incident, sanction or referral must have its actual writing, authority and send mapped for that episode.
School administration maintains rule id, current wording and effective date. The teacher reads the original rule if the link is unclear. No new student monitoring or emotion inference is introduced.
One of five lookup units is obsolete-document navigation; four remain for reading. Existing access runtime earns no saving, and live interaction retains ninety-five units.
unknowns: Whether the current rule is already immediately accessible
Which events actually require an incident record
research_questions: Does the current-version link save any search during ordinary enforcement?

already_counted.description: Read the relevant rule and address the actual student conduct

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R99 gross1 less upkeep0.5 gives0.5. For an ambiguous rule requiring original-source navigation, lookup retains4.5 of5; gross0.5 less upkeep0.5 gives0. Direct enforcement keeps all its time.

steps.what: Read the actual behavioral and academic problem context before conferring
Confer with parents, teachers, counselors or administrators about resolving the student's problems
Write the actual agreed actions into the existing student support plan

tasks.design: Link existing pupil evidence and stable goal references in the support plan tool {OTHER}. The teacher and participants resolve the issue directly, and the teacher writes the actual classroom actions in the working support plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence links and stable goal references are repeatedly located and entered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record links and reference fields reduce those small clerical costs.
tasks.still_hard: A workable resolution depends on the pupil's context and the participants' cooperation.
tasks.human_edge: Listen to conflicting perspectives and agree support that can actually be delivered.

ambition.what: Professional and family responsibilities remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked support-plan fields can reduce reference work without resolving a child's behavioral or academic problem automatically.

assumptions: Boundary includes preparation, actual conference and the real classroom support plan used by the teacher. No extra minutes or external message is invented. Formal specialist plans or authorized support decisions need their actual routes if present.

Teachers and authorized support staff produce existing evidence and goals through normal work. Participants supply the actual actions in s2; the teacher captures them in s3. Missing facts require source reading, not automatic inference.

s1 removes1.8 units of repeated navigation, retaining13.2 for source reading. s3 removes two units of stable goal references, retaining eighteen for actual action wording and checking. The ordinary save is negligible, unchanged and ungated.
unknowns: Whether a working support plan is maintained for these conferences
Which evidence the teacher may access
research_questions: Can stable reference reuse avoid copying obsolete support actions?

already_counted.description: Read context, confer directly and write actual support actions

incremental.description: Maintain restricted support links and repair stale goal references

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R96.2 gross3.8 less upkeep1.5 gives2.3. For changed support needs, context reading retains14.5 of15 and plan writing19 of20, with conference65 unchanged. Gross1.5 less upkeep1.5 gives0.

tasks.short: Plan and schedule lessons with colleagues

steps.what: Read approved curricula and current lesson scheduling constraints
Confer with other staff to choose lessons promoting learning
Write the actual shared lesson plan from the staff's agreed approach

loop.purpose: Draft the agreed lesson approach into the existing planning format
loop.input: Staff-selected lesson approach and approved curriculum
loop.output: Plan preserving agreed objectives and activities
loop.check: Teacher checks every activity, sequencing decision and intended learning against the actual staff agreement and curriculum
loop.stop: Missing decisions or changed educational meaning require manual writing; one redraft maximum
loop.why_not_simpler: The agreed approach includes case-specific teaching prose beyond fixed fields

steps.what: Compare proposed lesson times with fixed staff and room availability
Check the complete lesson plan and final schedule against the staff agreement
Publish the checked lesson schedule in the actual shared calendar

tasks.design: Use native curriculum links in {DOCS}, a bounded draft of the staff's chosen plan, and fixed conflict checks in {CALENDAR}. The teacher checks the complete plan and exact schedule before its real shared-calendar publication, whose already small time is retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing the agreed plan and manually comparing availability repeat work after the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Constrained drafting and native calendar conflict checks handle those separate clerical steps.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues must agree a coherent educational sequence and workable allocation.
tasks.human_edge: Choose teaching activities with colleagues and recognize educational trade-offs.

ambition.what: Compare a second feasible lesson sequence before choosing the shared plan.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound plan drafting and fixed calendar conflict checks can reduce post-meeting work while educational agreement remains human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual staff planning, the shared working lesson plan and real schedule publication. This case assumes the participating teacher is the existing authorized calendar coordinator; no new supervisory approval is invented.

Curriculum staff maintain goal wording; existing calendar owners produce availability. The teacher captures actual staff choices while writing s3, with any extra draft input or missing availability repair funded below. No meeting transcript or inferred pupil model is assumed.

s1 removes three units of navigation. s3 retains fifteen units for factual writing, semantic checks and corrections. s4 replaces actual manual conflict comparison only where native checks are not already used; existing runtime earns no saving.

s5 checks the final plan and schedule after both exist. Any changed time, plan or participant voids publication authorization. Publication is an actual operative calendar action, not an author save; its tiny one-unit time stays fully retained. Ordinary DOCS save within s3 is negligible and ungated.
unknowns: Whether the calendar already checks conflicts
Who publishes the actual agreed schedule
How much plan prose must be rewritten
research_questions: Can the final schedule remain bound to the staff-agreed lesson sequence?

already_counted.description: Read constraints, confer, review the shared plan, check final schedule and publish it

incremental.description: Repair incompatible availability fields, difficult plan drafts and curriculum links

approvals.approved_version: Exact lesson plan, times, rooms and participants checked against staff agreement in s5

R96 gross4 less upkeep3 gives1. The actual publication carries no saving.
